meiji_transition.summary: Fukuoka Prefecture was set up in 1871; Kokura Prefecture (western Buzen) and Mizuma Prefecture (Chikugo) joined in 1876.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Fukuoka = Chikuzen + Chikugo + western Buzen; eastern Buzen (Nakatsu, Usa) went to Ōita, so 'Buzen' was split in two.

history_timeline.title: Dazaifu
history_timeline.summary: Dazaifu governed Kyūshū and handled foreign relations — 'the distant court'; Sugawara no Michizane was exiled here in 901.

history_timeline.title: The Mongol defense wall
history_timeline.summary: Mongol fleets attacked in 1274 and 1281; the shogunate built a stone wall along Hakata Bay and set up the Chinzei Tandai in Hakata.

history_timeline.title: Kyūshū tandai and Hakata merchants
history_timeline.summary: Imagawa Ryōshun, as Kyūshū tandai, subdued the Southern Court's forces; Hakata thrived on trade with Ming China and Korea, fought over by the Ōuchi and Shōni.

history_timeline.title: The struggle for Kyūshū
history_timeline.summary: The Ōtomo, Ryūzōji and Shimazu fought for northern Kyūshū, and Tachibana Muneshige became famous for loyalty and valor; after subduing Kyūshū in 1587, Hideyoshi replanned Hakata ('Taikō machiwari').

history_timeline.title: Kuroda, 520,000 koku
history_timeline.summary: Kuroda Nagamasa was given Chikuzen and built Fukuoka Castle; samurai 'Fukuoka' and merchant 'Hakata' stood side by side as twin towns.

history_timeline.title: Industry and gateway
history_timeline.summary: The government-run Yawata Steel Works opened in 1901, laying the foundation of Japan's heavy industry; Fukuoka became a gateway city facing Asia.

landmarks.name: Dazaifu Tenmangū
landmarks.note: Shrine of Michizane, god of learning

dialect.name: Hakata dialect
dialect.features: '-to?', '-bai' and '-ken'; 'suitō yo' (I like you) is hailed as the cutest confession in Japan.

guide.opening: This humble interpreter of Dutch at Dejima has come to Hakata on official business. Dazaifu here was 'the distant court' that ran all of Kyūshū's foreign affairs — shall I tell you of Sugawara no Michizane?

regional_meme.title: Capital of Kyūshū
regional_meme.text: Fukuoka people assume Fukuoka is the capital of Kyūshū — the other six prefectures: who agreed to that?

regional_meme.title: Hakata vs. Fukuoka
regional_meme.text: The station is 'Hakata' but the city is 'Fukuoka' — the Meiji-era vote on the city's name still rankles with Hakata people.

hero_persona.name: Tachibana Muneshige
hero_persona.title: 'Peerless in the West'
hero_persona.opening_line: I am Tachibana Muneshige. Lord Hideyoshi called me 'peerless in the west'. I lost my lands after Sekigahara and returned to Yanagawa twenty years later — all my life I believed in one word: righteousness.
hero_persona.tone_prompt: composed and resolute, modest and principled; speaks of his father-in-law Tachibana Dōsetsu with deep respect

ramen.toppings: Chashu, wood-ear mushrooms, scallions, pickled ginger, sesame
ramen.highlight: Order your noodle firmness, like 'barikata' — then ask for a 'kaedama' refill

sake.taste_profile: Rich & sweet: an old house in Kyūshū's sweet-sake tradition
